summary: Retested CRITICAL native auth ticket flow on Linux Electron runtime copy. Device register 401 is fixed after ticket authorize exchange, and ticket machine-binding + one-time use checks passed. However, native browser open lifecycle is still unstable in this run (lease opens then is released quickly, renderer context closed before full assertions).

critical.issue: Lease acquires (200) but is released almost immediately in tested flow, preventing stable native WebContentsView verification from completing.

minor.issue: Invalid short ticket returns 422 schema validation (expected). This was observed in post-logout negative check.

ui_bugs.issue: Runtime state remained 'Navegador fechado' in one run and close button stayed disabled; in latest run renderer/page context closed before runtime checks.

integration_issues.flow: Desktop authorize/register -> open creator native browser
integration_issues.issue: Auth ticket exchange and register now succeed, but full open verification is flaky/unstable due rapid lease release and/or app context close before assertions complete.

action_items: Investigate why native open flow does not stay open long enough for deterministic assertions (lease created then promptly deleted in logs).
Instrument BrowserWorkspace/main.cjs event sequence around route navigation and open() calls to detect duplicate/overlapping opens and forced close paths.
Re-run Linux native smoke after stabilizing open lifecycle; then validate WebContentsView /api/health stand-in load, non-zero bounds, and session separation evidence.
Windows runtime and actual Privacy page remain unvalidated in this retest.
critical_code_review_comments: Main retest confirms auth architecture shift is working: /desktop/auth/ticket + /desktop/auth/exchange and native token-gated register path now return success.
Observed backend evidence includes initial register 401 followed by ticket issuance/exchange and subsequent register 200, matching intended fallback/authorize path.
Open-flow instability likely lies in desktop runtime lifecycle/timing, not ticket issuance itself; backend showed /desktop/leases 200 then immediate DELETE in same scenario.

rca of the issue: RCA (current evidence): Native auth fix is effective for register path (ticket issue/exchange + register approved). Remaining failure is in native browser open stabilization: backend logs show lease POST 200 followed by fast DELETE, while UI/runtime assertions either stay closed or renderer closes. Repro: launch isolated Electron app, login, ticket checks, authorize, register, create TEMP_NATIVE, navigate to /navegador/<temp_id>. Mitigation: add deterministic tracing around BrowserWorkspace auto-open effect and CreatorBrowser.open()/close() generation transitions to isolate premature close trigger.
